dossier.architecture: Mecanum collector, turreted two-position-hood shooter and conventional ratchet/telescope traversal climb.

subsystems.drivetrain: Drivetrain model not detailed in this walkthrough; technical cross-check remains necessary.
subsystems.intake: Wide mecanum intake centers moving cargo; reinforced after Waterloo impact damage.
subsystems.transfer: Vertical conveyor and upper color/beam-break sensing sequence balls before shooting.
subsystems.scoring: Turret turns approximately 175 degrees each way; vision distance chooses speed and two hood states.
subsystems.endgame: Ratchet hooks support the robot while telescopic arms reach the next rung; later quick low-rung option.
subsystems.controls: Wrong-color rejection changes turret/shot; delayed second-ball feed preserves classification and recovery.

versions: Intake strengthened after Waterloo; removed unnecessary centering wheels. Added white acquisition LEDs and low-rung hang.
dossier.analysis: The drive team explicitly weighs a final scoring cycle against traversal time and alliance climb needs. This is a useful model for comparing marginal points rather than always executing the maximum climb.
limits: Reported performance and prototype history are attributed to the source; not every intermediate revision is recoverable.

context_documents.title: 2022-2056 · Climb-or-shoot is a partner-dependent allocation decision
context_documents.body:
# 2022-2056: Climb-or-shoot is a partner-dependent allocation decision

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A wide collector centers moving cargo and was reinforced after impact damage. A vertical conveyor/color stage feeds a roughly ±175-degree turret with two hood states. The interview reports a roughly ten-to-fifteen-second best climb range.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly says reliable traversal partners can make continued shooting the preferable assignment.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

The comparison must include travel, capture, retries and available cargo, not only mechanism lift time. This demonstrates marginal task value in 2022 without making any claim that its climb incentive matches 2026.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure scored output during the entire climb interval and validate shared-climb reliability before fixing the alliance’s endgame allocation.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/yiXl7dlhDzY](https://youtu.be/yiXl7dlhDzY)

source_reviews.title: OP Robotics team interview at FIRST Championship
source_reviews.locator: 1:31–3:08 collector; 3:08–4:30 cargo sensing; 4:30–5:52 shot; 5:52–7:55 climb and alliance choices
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. Technical details are attributed to team speakers. No visual inspection claimed.
source_reviews.facts: Team describes self-centering, separation for color reads, two-position hood thresholds, climb sequence and conditional endgame choices.
source_reviews.limitations: Times and performance reports are attributed to the team. Some color terminology in automatic captions is ambiguous.

source_reviews.title: OP Robotics team history
source_reviews.review_basis: Read team specifications and followed the adjacent image link
source_reviews.facts: Names the robot Declaration and documents its tank drive, wheel count and dimensions.
source_reviews.limitations: Specifications and one overview image do not resolve subsystem geometry.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Declaration paired a six-wheel single-speed tank chassis with a yawing launcher, a self-centering floor pickup and a traversal climber. The turret gave the scoring tool a separate heading while the drivetrain maneuvered, while queue logic made it possible to handle consecutive cargo of different colors through one launch path. The team used climb depth as a tactical choice rather than committing to the same endgame in every match.
source_review.piece_flow: Oppositely oriented mecanum intake wheels center a bouncing cargo before it rises on the conveyor. A lower beam break signals pickup to the drive team with a white LED flash. A spaced queue carries pieces past an upper beam break and color sensor. The first piece can be classified before firing, and the next is delayed for its own read. Opposing cargo goes through the launcher on an intentionally offset trajectory.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The official team page lists a 32 by 28 inch footprint and a six-wheel tank drive. The tower puts the upper sensor near the turret feed and combines stationary approach with moving launcher packaging. The team credits experience routing the 2020 turret umbilical for widening the available rotation on Declaration. Rung transfers reuse two sets of arms rather than requiring one tool per rung.

subsystems.name: Floor intake and drive
subsystems.construction: Six 4-inch tread wheels on the tank chassis and mecanum contact wheels at the collector.
subsystems.operation: The mirrored rollers move an off-center cargo inward toward the conveyor. The operator also calls cargo the driver cannot see.
subsystems.team_rationale: Capture balls that are still bouncing or scattered after exiting the hub.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The centering claim depends on the actual approach speed and contact direction. Check what happens when the ball only touches the edge roller or meets the bumper first.
subsystems.interfaces: Bumper, conveyor entry, field sight lines and impact load path.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect intake straightness, bearings and the transition after wall strikes.
subsystems.unknowns: Roller geometry, speeds and capture envelope.

subsystems.name: Queue and color sensing
subsystems.construction: Conveyor with lower and upper beam breaks and upper color sensing.
subsystems.operation: The lower break triggers pickup feedback. Software leaves separation and delays the second release so the color reading belongs to the correct ball.
subsystems.team_rationale: Recover acquisition awareness behind field obstructions and classify each ball in time.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Separation is a sensing requirement as much as a packaging choice. Variable ball friction can collapse a time-based gap, so test mixed-color sequences in both orders.
subsystems.interfaces: Collector, sensors, driver LEDs and turret shot commands.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test stuck beam breaks, dirty optics, reversed feed and a second ball creeping into view.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact thresholds, optical layout and fallback behavior.

subsystems.name: Launcher
subsystems.construction: Limelight-guided turret and two-position hood. Team reports 175 degrees of rotation each way.
subsystems.operation: Range sets flywheel speed. The hood switches at an upper range threshold and returns at a lower threshold.
subsystems.team_rationale: Reuse the 2020 turret concept while gaining rotation and reliable range coverage.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Threshold separation limits repeated switching around the boundary. Test both hood modes across their overlap, including a range dropout during feed.
subsystems.interfaces: Umbilical, field heading, conveyor and wheel speed control.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect bend radius and travel margin. Test edge-of-travel aim and intentional reject trajectories.

subsystems.name: Hangar climber
subsystems.construction: Ratchet hooks and pivoting telescopic hooks.
subsystems.operation: Catch the mid rung, move the extending hooks to the next bar and repeat load transfers. Team describes a later fast low-rung option.
subsystems.team_rationale: Retain an endgame scoring fallback when partners cannot cover the climb.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Compare added climb points with the expected value of another scoring cycle, including the time to approach and verify engagement.
subsystems.interfaces: Hangar geometry, hook sets, moving arm envelope and operator timing.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check partial catches and load release between hook sets.
subsystems.unknowns: Per-event success rates and full loaded climb timing distribution.

revisions: After Waterloo the team strengthened a bent intake and removed two mecanum wheels. It also added pickup indication after the first event and reported adding a low-rung hang option.
transferable_principles: Use per-piece sensing and explicit spacing when shared hardware must route mixed cargo. Distinguish fast best-case climbs from reliable late-match plans.
disconfirming_conditions: Under an electric-only, fixed-azimuth requirement, the historical hood and turret interfaces need new actuation and targeting. Flexible or irregular payloads may not self-center on the same rollers.
remaining_gaps: Older dossier used for navigation. Reviewed interview and team specifications. No verified 2022 source code or dated CAD dimensions were available.
